newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt wants to expand industry/union talks.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt wants to expand industry/union talks.

text.p: German economics minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Thursday he wants to extend his roundtable talks with union and industry leaders in an effort to lower unemployment and improve the country's competitiveness.

Over the last two years Rexrodt has brought unions and employer groups together 13 times to discuss labour costs, taxes, economic growth, technology and other factors affecting Germany's outlook for jobs and economic growth.
Rexrodt would like to continue the series with groups from other industries -- expecially since many unions and employers have clashed while hashing out new contracts in recent months.
Unions had resisted attempts to apply a new law allowing employers to pay workers 80 percent of their regular pay for sick time.

Rexrodt, a member of the Free Democracts, the junior partner in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition, will next meet with trade and commerce representatives on January 15 and electronics industry unions and employers on January 21.
Past talks have included groups from the auto, chemical, textil, shipbuilding, steel, machinery, construction, ceramics, furniture and services industries.

Unemployment reached a record 4.1 million in November, and was expected to rise to around 4.5 million in the first half of 1997. Bonn has set a goal of halving unemployment by the year 2000, but its "Alliance for Jobs" with unions and industry collapsed last year.
At the same time, Germany has not fared well against international competitors, losing some of its share of world exports.
In 1997 it was expected to see exports grow six percent even though world trade should rise 7.5 percent, according to the German Economics Institute.
